messages:
Sasha: Heads up — onboarding Tempest11B (opt-arch variant) into the int4 pipeline and seeing a weird warmup-induced loop in summarization outputs. short repro in a sec. :eyes:
Pranav: ugh, warmup loop? like repeated phrases after a few tokens?
Sasha: Exactly. Float32 baseline is fine. Int4 quantized run starts generating repeating chunks after ~120 tokens. Happens across beam/greedy.
Anya: can you paste the small repro + config? we should check kv-cache indices and any prefix caching that's conditional on dtype.
Sasha: repro curl ->
```
curl -s -X POST https://local-redwood-sim/api/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' -d '{"model":"tempest-11b-opt","prompt":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":400,"temperature":0.0,"quant":"int4"}'
```
Sasha: quick sample output (int4): 
"The study shows that the model found that the model found that the model found that..." — loops phrase. Float32: fine.
Miguel: any diffs in rotary/positional handling on conversion? Tempest uses a hybrid rotary+absolute pos concat we added last month. If quant path accidentally zeros small rot-freq terms, head responses could collapse.
Pranav: good call. Also check per-head scale clipping during quant kernel fallback. We had a patch that clamps rotary frequencies for small dtypes.
Anya: pinging eval-bot to run a quick headwise signal check and log attention entropy over tokens for both float32 and int4.
Sasha: thanks. Attaching the conversion log excerpt: 
```
[convert] layer 36 head 8: q/k scale mean 0.00012 -> clipped to 0.0 in int4 path
[convert] rotary_freqs min 1.2e-06 clipped->0.0
```
Miguel: clipping rotary freqs to zero would effectively remove positional modulation for some heads — that can produce repetition. Is that clipping from our quant calibration script or the runtime kernel?
Pranav: looks like the calibration script's per-tensor min/max heuristic set empty ranges for tiny-magnitude tensors. We added an "aggressive min-span" option to avoid NaN ranges, maybe it backfired.
Anya: eval-bot: run results?
eval-bot: Ran headwise attention entropy probe on seed=42. Summary:
- float32: mean entropy per head=3.9 bits, variance 0.8
- int4 (current conversion): mean entropy=1.2 bits, variance 0.2
- note: heads 8, 12, 19 show near-zero rotary freqs after quant clamps.
Pranav: that matches the generate behaviour. Lower entropy -> deterministic loop.
Sasha: quick experiment: re-convert with "min-span=1e-5" and keep per-head scaling preserved. I pushed artifact to /tmp/artifacts/tempest-int4-minspan1e-5.pt and tested -> no loop on same prompt.
Miguel: great. Can you run full eval harness (summaries dataset) to get rouge/bertscore diffs vs float? small reg check.
Sasha: running now. Preliminary: int4 (orig) ROUGE-1=0.31, ROUGE-L=0.27; int4 (min-span fix) ROUGE-1=0.45, ROUGE-L=0.41, float32=0.47/0.43.
Anya: that's promising — quality mostly restored. We should avoid global clamps in calibration and instead fallback to per-head symmetric quant params or mixfloat for tiny tensors.
Pranav: action items: 1) revert aggressive global clamp in conversion script; 2) add per-tensor min-span floor of 1e-6 with headwise override; 3) add unit test: generate on long-summary prompt and assert no repeated phrase >3x.
Miguel: I'll add a runtime guard too that rejects zeroed rotary_freqs and falls back to float compute for that head.
Sasha: I'll open PR with conversion fix + results + benchmark artifacts. attaching run ids: run-20260322-tempest-int4-minspan and run-20260322-tempest-int4-orig.
Anya: nice. Also log tokenizer note: tempests' tokenizer normalizes U+200D sequences; check NFKC normalization parity across conversion pipeline. That can shift token boundaries and exacerbate repetition when pos encodings differ.
Sasha: good catch — tokenization parity confirmed in these runs (same byte seq). will add a quick tokenizer hash to artifact.
Pranav: thanks team. If CI passes with the new unit test and bench numbers, let's promote this conversion recipe to the int4 catalog and mark the old artifact deprecated.
Sasha: updating thread with PR link shortly. :thumbsup:
